What distinguishes peremptory norms from other principles of customary law?
A: ["Peremptory norm"]
Q: What distinguishes peremptory norms from other principles of customary law?
A: "Peremptory norms, also known as \"jus cogens,\" are distinguished from other principles of customary law by their non-derogable nature. Unlike ordinary customary law, which can be altered or violated by states through treaties or local customs, peremptory norms cannot be violated by any state. They hold a higher normative force and cannot be set aside or overridden by any agreements or practices that do not possess the same level of authority. This means that peremptory norms are universally binding and must be adhered to by all states, regardless of their consent."
